# Quantum Readout Rank Threshold

This repository studies how many identical copies a fixed measurement must process jointly to retain a uniform fraction of local SLD quantum Fisher information.

## Study route

- Selected educational anchor and notation/source bridge: learning/ANCHOR.md
- Complete common understanding map, M01–M30, with dependencies and source pointers: learning/MILESTONES.md
- Reader entrypoint and focused routes: learning/README.md

The single educational anchor is Demkowicz-Dobrzanski, Gorecki and Guta, Multi-parameter estimation beyond Quantum Fisher Information, J. Phys. A 53, 363001 (2020), arXiv:2001.11742v2, shared with Calibrated-Quantum-Readout. It supplies score, SLD, nuisance and collective-estimation foundations. The project supplies the fixed-rank design, Schur, coherent-width and exact Haar arguments. The 30-milestone map has 10 background and 20 narrative milestones.

## Read by question

- Exact experiment, allowed apparatus and rank classification: science/model.md
- Two-copy SWAP and projective 3-design construction, every tangent component and circuit resources: science/two-copy-readout.md
- Exact continuous-Haar pair information for all seven rank-two qutrit tangent directions, strict near-boundary comparison with the adaptive one-copy ceiling, and its implementation limits: science/haar-pair-readout.md
- Arbitrary-outcome finite-block converse, Schur multiplicities and uniform normalized-effect argument: science/finite-block-obstruction.md
- Exact leading spectral-information coefficient, attaining binary measurement and limit order: science/singular-information.md
- Growing coherent block width, three-row Schur achievability, dominant-ray upper bound and half-information width: science/copy-width-crossover.md
- Calibration, coherent block size, persistent memory and local versus global loss: science/interpretation.md
- Primary antecedents and matched comparisons: references/RELATED_WORK.md
- Bibliographic metadata: references/references.bib
- Executed finite checks, dependencies and boundaries: verification/README.md

Use the source definitions. J is single-copy SLD information, J_2=2J, and all input copies and measurement outcomes are charged. For the rank-three scalar tangent, the fixed-width coefficient takes p to zero with k and eta fixed. The growing-width limit takes eta to zero with p/eta tending to zero and k eta tending to a, giving the optimal fraction 1-(1-exp(-a))/a for 0<a<infinity, extended continuously to the endpoints. Half information has leading block width 1.593624260.../eta. The local scalar theorem leaves full-matrix and finite-sample risk questions open.

For a connected account, start at README.md and science/README.md, then follow the model, finite-design construction, exact Haar comparison, finite-block converse, singular-coefficient calculation, coherent-width theorem and interpretation. The general statements rely on the written proofs. Run the finite checks in verification/README.md.

The sister Calibrated-Quantum-Readout repository owns the calibrated single-copy optimum and science/paid-calibration.md, which analyzes complete pilot transcripts and separate strong/weak eigenvector errors. This repository owns the exact Haar pair comparison. Its full-model fraction is greater than one quarter sufficiently near the rank-one boundary, tending to one quarter; no sharp finite-Clifford constant, universal paid-calibration crossover or finite-sample risk ordering is asserted. Scientific counterpart: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Calibrated-Quantum-Readout/blob/67071bb77deb232a02d48968d7c52adfd817f367/science/paid-calibration.md .
